answer: I built a 6-spin chain (J=1, h=1, all spins starting up, time 1) as a 4-step Trotter circuit. I made two stretched copies by gate folding (each U becomes U, then U-inverse, then U), which gives 3 times and 5 times the gates and the same ideal answer. I submitted all 3 as one job to garnet:mock (job 01a16062-6f8e-7099-98a1-367c6171c448, 1000 shots each). It completed, which shows the circuits are valid for Garnet. Mock counts are random, so I did not use them for physics. I ran the same 3 circuits on IQMFakeGarnet (20000 shots each) to get noisy magnetizations. They were 0.112 at noise 1, 0.071 at noise 3, and 0.049 at noise 5. The ideal is 0.187. More noise pulls the value further from the ideal, in a smooth way. Fitting a quadratic through the three points and reading it at noise 0 (Richardson extrapolation) gives 0.139. A straight line gives 0.125. So extrapolation recovered about 2.5 times more of the lost signal than the raw value, but did not fully reach the ideal. The principle: if you can make noise bigger on purpose and see how the answer changes, you can extend the trend back to zero noise. The cost is more gates and more shots, and the result depends on the fit.
